title: Resilience audit: cross-region amplification during failover exposed circuit-breaker asymmetry
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Summary: During an automated cross-region failover triggered by a control-plane maintenance window (2026-03-01 02:00 UTC), traffic reshaping caused an amplification effect in the secondary region. The amplification overran circuit breaker thresholds and caused sustained SLO misses for tail latency (95th/99th). This ticket consolidates the investigation findings, temporary mitigations, and a prioritized set of follow-up action items to prevent recurrence and restore SLO headroom.

Scope: Platform serving runtime (request routing, circuit-breakers), control-plane failover orchestration, and regional autoscaling/load-shedding integration.

Primary goals: 1) capture timeline and root cause evidence, 2) document temporary mitigations and production observations, 3) define concrete engineering tasks with owners, estimates, and due dates, 4) coordinate monitoring and runbook updates for future events.
timeline: 2026-03-01 01:45 UTC: Planned maintenance window announced for control-plane region us-east-1. Automated failover policy set to active for 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-01 02:00 UTC: Control plane began orchestrated failover; most traffic shifted to us-west-2. Initial routing transition completed within 45s.
2026-03-01 02:01 UTC: Unexpected request fanout observed from several tenant shards; per-tenant routing multiplier increased due to simultaneous reconnect attempts and KV cache cold misses.

2026-03-01 02:02-02:10 UTC: Secondary region circuit-breakers tripped asymmetrically (some clusters tripped earlier due to lower marker thresholds); automatic shedding kicked in but was insufficient to prevent SLO slippage at 95th/99th latencies.
2026-03-01 02:15 UTC: Emergency runbook invoked; traffic throttles enforced at the edge and partial rollback of some canary routing rules executed.
2026-03-01 03:00 UTC: Traffic patterns stabilized after manual interventions and incremental rebalancing; SLOs recovered to within target by 03:40 UTC.
2026-03-01 04:00 UTC: Post-event logs and traces collected; initial RCA kickoff scheduled for 2026-03-02.
root_causes: Circuit-breaker thresholds were heterogeneous across clusters and not aligned with observed cold-start amplification patterns, creating points of early trip that cascaded reroutes.
KV cache warmup during failover led to synchronous backend calls and a surge in per-request compute, amplifying tail latency.
Failover routing policy applied at control plane level lacked per-tenant smoothing; several high-concurrency tenants reissued a large number of parallel requests on reconnect.
Autoscaling and shedding policies in the target region had conservative trigger window settings and delayed actuation, which allowed latency to degrade before capacity responded.
mitigations_taken: Immediate: throttled new connections at the edge for top 20 tenants with highest reconnect rates (02:10–02:30 UTC).
Immediate: temporarily relaxed inter-cluster reroute multiplier to spread surge more evenly (02:18 UTC).
After-event: increased KV cache pre-warm windows for scheduled failovers and added pre-warm checklist item to maintenance playbooks (03-02).
Monitoring: created dashboard tile for cross-region reconnect rate and per-tenant reconnect multipliers.
comments: 2026-03-02 Priya Desai: Initial RCA draft added; focus on asymmetric circuit-breaker behavior + reconnect amplification. Next: validate metric histograms for top 10 affected clusters.

2026-03-03 Marcus Lee: Added heatmap of per-cluster trip-times to the artifact links. Early hypothesis: cluster-level CB markers are too low relative to cold-start tail. Planning spike to simulate cold KV misses in staging (estimate: 3d).

2026-03-04 Mei Chen (oncall): Live traffic replay in staging reproduced 2.3x amplification under reconnect storm. Verified that increasing CB headroom prevents early trips but increases backend load—tradeoff discussion needed.
2026-03-06 Anders Holm (SRE): Observability enhancement PR submitted: alert for reconnect-rate > 1.5x baseline with per-tenant tagging (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4217).
2026-03-08 Product note from Priya: Coordinate with Growth to surface customer-facing postmortem for top affected orgs (private outreach).
2026-03-10 Marcus Lee: Action plan prioritized; creating sub-issues for circuit-breaker harmonization, pre-warm automation, and autoscaler tuning.
